ptl_001: You can recognise it as the large copper beech standing alone as the centrepiece of the lawn. It stands at the main entrance to PSU's Millar Library, on SW Park Ave.
ptl_002: You can recognise it by its mottled plane bark, often mistaken locally for a sycamore. It stands in the street planting strip at the corner of SW Park Ave and SW Main St.
ptl_004: You can recognise it as the walnut the school building was built around rather than through, close enough to the freeway to hear it. It stands on the Lincoln High School lawn at the corner of SW Salmon and SW 14th.
ptl_008: You can recognise it by its towering height, over 45 metres, growing straight out of a residential street verge. It stands at the entrance to a driveway on SW Patton Rd.
ptl_009: You can recognise it by a large stone marking it beside the trail, and by looking straight up, since it is Portland's tallest tree by far. It stands on the Lower Macleay spur trail, past the Witch's Castle ruin.
ptl_010: You can recognise it by its narrow, feathery conifer crown, turning copper and dropping bare late in the year. It stands in Hoyt Arboretum, near SW Bray Ln.
